critical_code_review_comments: engine.py::claim_level — leaderboard_cache.delete_many({}) at the end of a successful non-idempotent claim (line 315) is the CORRECT freshness invalidation; verified empty right after claim. Idempotent replays skip this branch which is fine since the underlying user state didn't change.

engine.py::claim_level idempotency path — when ulp.current_level_id != level_id, the engine looks up any prior success claim for (user, level) regardless of level_version and returns its cached response. This correctly handles the 'replay after already advancing to Explorer' case, but if a level's config_version bumps and the user re-hits the same level_id, the returned response is from the OLD version. Acceptable for current spec (versions rarely re-target the same completed level).

ProgressCard.jsx — claimingRef double-submit guard is correctly checked BEFORE setClaiming(true) so an out-of-order state update cannot bypass it. finally-block guarantees both refs are cleared even if load() throws (comment says refetch failure ≠ claim failure — verified true via try/catch on line 123).

CelebrationModal.jsx — Escape-to-close listener uses onClose from prop; parent passes () => setCelebration(null). Click-on-backdrop also closes via outer onClick; inner card stopPropagation is correct. .or-modal-card overrides `backdrop-filter:none !important` which is what actually kills the black-screen stacking issue on iOS Safari.

ProgressionBadges.jsx — the or-progression-claimed listener is set up in the same useEffect as the initial loadAll, but the cleanup only removes the listener, not any in-flight fetches. Not a bug, just an observation — if the user navigates away mid-refetch a stale setState is possible (React swallows the warning in production).
Leaderboard cache TTL is 300s and the /me endpoint uses the same _cached_rows source — this is why leaderboards/me and /leaderboards rank match exactly. Good design; keep it.
